record.original_question: Given a general T-periodic Riccati differential equation x' = A_2(t)x^2 + A_1(t)x + A_0(t), find effective criteria that determine whether it has a continuum of periodic solutions or exactly 2, 1, or 0 limit cycles.

evidence.quote: Problem 5. For a general T periodic Riccati differential equation dx/dt = A2(t)x^2 + A1(t)x + A0(t) give effective criteria to know when it has a continuum of periodic solutions, or it has exactly 2, 1 or 0 limit cycles.

artifact.category_tag: Periodic Riccati equations and limit cycles
artifact.status_search_result: A 2025 preprint addresses a "Weak-Coppel problem" for a class of Riccati differential equations, indicating that the general problem of giving effective criteria to distinguish the four cases (continuum of periodic solutions, or 2, 1, 0 limit cycles) remains active and unsolved in full generality. Existing results give partial criteria (e.g., via monodromy/discriminant analysis or harmonic balance) but no complete effective characterization is known.

status_evidence.title: Weak-Coppel problem for a class of Riccati differential equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work studies a Coppel-type problem for periodic Riccati equations, addressing criteria for the number of limit cycles.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of effective criteria for the number of limit cycles of periodic Riccati equations remains an active research topic with only partial results.

status_evidence.title: On Periodic Solutions of the Periodic Riccati Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies existence and stability of periodic solutions of Riccati equations with periodic coefficients.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial criteria for periodic solutions are available in the literature.
